definitions.explanation: One of the most common Japanese surnames, consistently ranking first or second by population. Often used as a default "sample" name in textbook examples and forms, similar to "Smith" in English.

examples.japanese: {佐藤|さとう}さん、⟦こんにちは→こんにちは：02839_konnichiha⟧。
⟦クラス→クラス：01084_kurasu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{佐藤|さとう}さん⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: There are two Satos in the class.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧いちばん⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦{苗字|みょうじ}→苗字：14012_myouji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{佐藤|さとう}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: Sato is said to be the most common surname in Japan.

notes:
A surname so common it is often used as a stand-in name in language textbooks, sample forms, and demonstration materials.

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
さとう is also the reading for several unrelated words. In context the meaning is usually clear:
- ⟦{砂糖|さとう}→砂糖：00884_satou⟧: sugar
- ⟦{左党|さとう}→左党：23468_satou⟧: left-wing party; (idiomatically) drinker

CULTURAL NOTE:
The origin is generally traced to the {藤原|ふじわら} clan, with {佐|さ} referring to the {左衛門尉|さえもんのじょう} office. Today the name is most concentrated in northeastern Japan (⟦{東北|とうほく}→東北：27542_touhoku⟧). It alternates with ⟦{鈴木|すずき}→鈴木：09530_suzuki⟧ for the top spot in nationwide surname rankings.
